rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Judged fresh, not re-filed, per dispatch instructions. Both flagged spans are the sole bolded element on their slide (satisfies the numeric ≤1-per-slide budget) and both function as a distilled one-line takeaway rather than as a bolded LEAD on a bulleted list (the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture shape rule 9's own violation-shape clause names) — so neither is the shouted-paragraph pattern the rule was written against. But the two spans are not equivalent to each other, and the corpus precedent (prework.md line 22: "**Separate tasks off your backlog. Not slices of one.**", 9 words, one clean contrast) sets a bar the two spans here sit on either side of. Chunk 2 "Prework" line 14: "**A feature you could ship in a few hours. Not a quarter-long epic.**" (13 words, same [instruction]. Not [X]. shape as the prework precedent, single clause pair, one idea) — reads as a scannable sizing handle, not a shout. PASS by consistency with the passed corpus precedent; not re-flagged. Chunk 10 "Bring to Module 4" line 89: "**One scoped task you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit: a real slice. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than an epic.**" (23 words, roughly 2.5x the precedent) stacks two distinct claims under one bold span — a send-off-vs-nudge distinction AND a typo-fix/epic sizing bracket, joined by a colon and a second sentence. That's compound, not a single distilled line; it reads as paragraph elaboration wearing bold rather than a handle a student re-finds by squinting. Harm rule 9 exists to prevent: bold that stops carrying signal because it carries too much — here a single bold span asks the eye to parse two ideas at once, which is closer to the shouted-paragraph failure than to the prework precedent it sits beside in the same corpus. REVISE, not blocking (rule 9 carries no blocking sub-item here per the judge template's blocking partition — todo only). Rule question for the maintainer, not a repeat flag: check_slides.md §9 currently defines the legitimate case only as named laws/governors/coined terms/checklist item names (≲5-word sub-span), which neither this file's nor prework.md's callouts literally satisfy — both are full imperative sentences, not coined terms. If the intended shape also covers a short DISTILLED-TAKEAWAY callout (a standalone one-line paragraph, single clause pair, sole bold element on its slide, functioning as the one thing to retain from the block above it), §9 should say so explicitly and give it a length/clause ceiling (the prework precedent argues for roughly ≤1 sentence, ≤2 clauses, ≤~15 words) so a callout that grows past one idea — like this file's Bring-to-Module-4 line — has a bright line to fail, instead of leaving each fire to eyeball two similarly-shaped spans and land on different verdicts.
